fatal_errors: No specific lightweight material or composition is identified.
The key intervention—spark plasma sintering of ball-milled MgAlTiVFeCo powder at 1000 °C—is not reconstructed.
The proposed mechanism omits densification, oxide barrier-phase precipitation, passive-film formation, chloride blocking, and diffusion-controlled oxidation.
No quantitative processing window, oxidation condition, corrosion condition, or target performance is provided.
Refractory HEAs are presented as lightweight candidates even though cited evidence E5 explicitly notes that most RHEAs have high density and poor high-temperature oxidation resistance.
explanation: The response offers only a broad claim that HEAs or RHEAs can provide good mechanical and thermal properties. It does not answer which material should be used and fails to identify MgAlTiVFeCo, its initial BCC powder state, or SPS at 1000 °C. It also misses the decisive outcomes of 96.7% relative density, 1235.5 HV hardness, improved oxidation kinetics, and superior NaCl corrosion resistance. The proposed experiment could test a generic alloying claim, but it lacks specified compositions, SPS temperatures, lower-temperature controls, oxidation-rate constants, and electrochemical measurements needed to discriminate the target mechanism. The citations support broad HEA property claims but do not support the asserted lightweight recommendation and contain an unacknowledged contradiction regarding RHEA density and oxidation behavior.
